abstract: Given the widespread use of electric vehicles, they can be used in their idle state to provide services when connected to the grid or supply power in islanded operation using the bidirectional charger. Today, when connected to the grid, reversible chargers employ grid-following control, and when operating in islanded conditions, they use constant voltage constant frequency control. However, limitations exist for both control strategies. In this context, grid-forming control can be used to operate in all cases. This paper showcases the potential of grid-forming control when applied to a reversible charger for different operation modes of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Substation Voltage Optimization Strategy in Traction Power Supply System with Bidirectional Converter Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The bidirectional converter device (BCD) can replace the traditional diode rectifier unit to both supply traction energy to the system and to recover regenerative braking energy. The operating characteristics of BCDs are controllable, and it is very important to study the impact on system energy saving. This paper is based on the application scheme of BCDs to completely replace diode rectifier units. The operating characteristics of the BCD are introduced, and the energy distribution of the system is analyzed. Taking the total energy consumption of the system as the objective function, a substation voltage optimization strategy is proposed considering the dynamic operation of trains. It can dynamically optimize the ratio of energy utilization through different paths, allocate the power of each substation. Finally, a multi-train scenario is carried out by Matlab. The simulation results prove that the proposed strategy can coordinate the power of each substation and reduce the system losses. The system energy utilization is increased by 1.77% compared to the constant voltage control.

articleTitle: Multi-Domain Simulation of Integrated Power Electronics Modules for EMC and EMI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This work presents a complete electromagnetic and circuital simulation flow able to determine and analyze the EMC and EMI phenomena, allowing the designer to detect potential concerns before the prototyping, thus reducing costs and time-to-market. An LLC resonant power converter application, featuring a STMicroelectronics SiC-based AcePack module, is adopted for verification purposes. The proposed simulation flow could be an essential tool to support the optimal design that will be addressed in future works.

articleTitle: Energy Evaluation of PV and ESS Integrated AC Railways for Suburban Trains
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper evaluates the energy consumption of PV and ESS integration into the AC railways. A mathematical model of the AC railway network, with PV and ESS control, is formulated and solves the network power flow. The output illustrates the voltage levels, power generation and the energy consumption of the substation. A case study is based on the standard settings of a 100 km rail route, where PV and ESS are integrated. Four integration scenarios are compared to highlight the improvement of voltage drops, power demand and energy consumption of the traction substation with the integration of both PV and ESS.

articleTitle: A 48V/360A Power Module-Based Paralleled-GaN Devices for Low-Voltage and High-Current Traction Inverter Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Gallium nitride GaN power semiconductors are gaining popularity in high-power traction inverter applications. The phase current can reach up to several hundred amps in such cases. Therefore, paralleling multiple GaN HEMT transistors is undoubtedly a solution for increasing power capability and reducing conduction losses. This paper proposes a highly integrated paralleled GANs power module design (100 V/360 A) based on an insulated metal substrate (IMS). The proposed design provides a low and symmetrical commutation loop inductance, high thermal conductivity, and a cost-effective solution. The double pulse test (DPT) experiment has been successfully implemented at 48V/325A to validate the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: A Simplified Analytical Approach for NVH Assessment of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The paper deals with NVH (Noise Vibration and Harshness) analysis of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Electric Motors (PMSMs) for automotive applications. A simplified analytical model is presented and used to simulate the acoustic emission of PMSMs. The simplified model is based on a 2D circular curved beam of generalized cross section. The input radial and tangential electromagnetic force distribution is computed by means of the Maxwell stress tensor. The differential equations describing the vibrational behavior of the curved beam are analytically solved and explicit, closed-form expressions of the vibration and sound pressure levels are derived. The novelty of the presented model relies in the introduction of the lever-arm effect induced by tangential electromagnetic forces in the stator vibration. The developed model is employed to compare different architectures of PMSMs, particularly referring to their NVH performances.

articleTitle: Effect of Rider Position on the Energy Consumption of an Electric Motorcycle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Unlike other transport vehicles, the rider of a motorcycle contributes to the change of frontal area and drag coefficient during riding as their position changes, and therefore, rider position can directly affect energy consumption. This manuscript systematically investigates the effects of variations in combined drag coefficient and frontal area on electric motorcycle (EM) range over the World Motorcycle Test Cycle (WMTC) 3.2 standard drive cycle. The combined drag coefficient and frontal area (CdA) values were measured in a full-scale wind tunnel using a rider who was fully kitted in separate leathers as opposed to single piece race suits. A vehicle longitudinal backwards-facing model was used to estimate the effect of different riding position on motorcycle energy consumption. A decrease of 30% in the product of drag coefficient (Cd) and frontal area (A) through changing from an upright to a tucked-in position leads to a decrease of up to 19% in terms of energy consumption.

articleTitle: Impact of Maximal Velocity and Acceleration on Energy Consumption of a Subway Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This article investigates the potential for energy savings in a subway vehicle by modifying the velocity reference (i.e., maximal velocity and maximal acceleration). The studied subway system is based on Line 1 of the city of Lille, France. Simulations reveals that a 20% reduction in reference velocity results in a 10.48% decrease in energy consumption while increasing travel time by 10.07%. Additionally, modifying the maximum acceleration does not have a significant effect, presenting 0.94% of energy reduction for a 20% reduction on the maximal acceleration value.

articleTitle: Constant Common-Mode Voltage Modulation Analysis and Implementation for a Dual Three-Phase Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation and implementation of a modified constant CMV SVPWM technique. In the literature, SVPWM techniques to reduce the CMV are proposed. However, these modulations present a complex implementation. This paper proposes a modulation with a much simpler implementation. The proposed modulation is compared in simulation with SVPWM-4L and Carrier-Based PWM SVPWM modulations regarding low-order harmonics, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{THD}_{i}$</tex> and CMV. The proposed hardware implementation is validated experimentally with dSPACE.

articleTitle: Efficiency Improvement of SPMSG in the Engine-Generator System of a PHEV Shown to be Compatible with an Optimal Operating Line
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical optimization scheme of a surface permanent magnet synchronous generator (SPMSG) for achieving maximum efficiency. The generator and engine are linked and the optimal operating line is identified. A genetic algorithm is combined with a mesh adaptive direct search to create an intelligent memetic algorithm used to find the maximum efficiency distribution of SPMSG compatible to the OOL. The proposed optimization scheme includes both electrical and mechanical losses. Efficiency accuracy is confirmed by the resultant efficiency map. A prototype based on an optimized model is experimentally validated and shown to be well-suited for an EGS of a PHEV.

articleTitle: Robust Control Method for Mitigating Disturbances Caused by Renewable Energy Sources in AC Railway Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In recent years railway section experts have concentrated on innovative solutions for increasing energy efficiency and especially on the connection of renewable energy sources (RES) into electric railway systems (ERSs). However, one of the main issues of such an integration is that increasing high-power RES connection to the railway grid will increase the probability of grid disturbances and cause instability and malfunction of devices. This paper presents a new control scheme for railway power flow controller (RPFC) to improve its dynamic and compensation performance by mitigating disturbances. A wavelet transform-based control method integrated with instantaneous reactive power theory is proposed to optimize the RPFC performance confronting the main power quality (PQ) issues of ERS. The accurate simulation results using MATLAB SIMULINK are provided to verify the theoretical analysis and reveal the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Prognostic and Health Management of an Aircraft Turbofan Engine Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: An aircraft's turbofan engine is essential to its operation. As with any component of a machine, engine components are subject to degradation and wear over time. This degradation can affect the performance of the engine and may lead to unexpected failures or decreased efficiency. To ensure proper maintenance, predicting its remaining useful life (RUL) is crucial. This paper presents a prediction framework for the RUL of aircraft engines using machine learning (ML) techniques, specifically a Deep Layer Recurrent Neural Network (DL-RNN) model. The proposed method is compared to other ML algorithms, such as Multilayer-Perceptron (MLP), Cascade Forward Neural Network (CFNN), and Nonlinear Auto Regressive Network with Exogenous Inputs (NARX), using two datasets provided by NASA. The results show that the DL-RNN model has better predictive precision compared to the other methodologies.

articleTitle: Torque Allocation and Energy Management Strategy for a Multi-Motor Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The 2023 edition of the IEEE VTS Motor Vehicles Challenge proposed to develop energy and mechanical management strategies for an electric vehicle (EV) equipped with three motors and a hybrid energy system based on fuel cells and batteries. The proposed strategy aimed to maximize the performance of the EV by making it possible to work the hybrid energy storage system, as much as possible, in its optimal efficiency range and by adequately allocating the total required torque among the three motors. The developed strategy achieved second place at the 2023 edition of the IEEE VTS Motor Vehicles Challenge.

articleTitle: Reduced Order Electromagnetic Thermal Coupled Model of EV PMSM for Digital Twin Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper establishes a digital twin (DT) model of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) for electric vehicle (EV) application. The model consists of two parts, namely the electromagnetic model and the thermal model. Both models are composed of geometric models, physical models, and behavioral models. Two models are then reduced through different reduction methods, thereby meeting the real-time computation requirements. By comparing with the simulation results of traditional finite element software, the accuracy of the reduced-order model is verified. Finally, the steps of constructing the electromagnetic thermal coupling digital twin model of PMSM are described with a specific example, which lays the foundation for the research of the motor DT.

articleTitle: Configuration Ratio of Grid-Following/Forming Control for High-Penetration Renewable Energy Integrated System Containing Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The charge-discharge between distributed generations and electric vehicles (EVs) will be an important component of the future development of EVs. In this paper, the optimal configuration ratio (CR) of grid-following/forming (GFL/GFM) control for high-penetration renewable energy integrated system containing EV is investigated: (1) The mathematical models for the grid-connected inverter and GFL/GFM control are elaborated, and five simulation cases with different CRs [CR: (100%, 75%, 50%, 25%, 0%)] are simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC. (2) The optimal CR is obtained through the comparative analysis of simulation results of different CRs under load disturbance /single phase-to-ground fault/island operation mode with corresponding evaluation indicators.

articleTitle: On the Development of a Diagnostic System for Condition Based Maintenance of Passenger Trains
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Condition Based Maintenance (CBM) is rapidly becoming an essential tool in the railway industry to reach new standards in the maintenance practice of rail vehicles. Health monitoring system are essential to reach this goal, nonetheless they are still lacking on most commercial trains. In this work a wireless monitoring system is developed to retrofit passenger vehicles with a cheap, easy to install and independent instrumentation. The architecture of the system and the main features of the wireless sensors are presented in the work. Exemplary data collected by the system in a field campaign on a passenger vehicle are proposed. These data can be used to monitor the vehicle dynamics and to perform diagnostic activities on the suspensions.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Effect of PAC2002 Tire Force Modelling on High-Power AWD Electric Vehicle Longitudinal Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive model for designing and analyzing high-power all-wheel-drive electric vehicles (HPAWD EVs), considering tire behaviour using the PAC2002 model with load-and-pressure dependent coefficients and vertical load transfers. Existing vehicle dynamics models use simple tire models that assume them to be rigid bodies leading to inflated results. The proposed model enables accurate simulation and analysis of longitudinal vehicle performance, providing insights into the relationship between vehicle and tire forces. The results show over 3% difference in 0–60 mph sprint time when comparing the PAC2002 model to the commonly used model. Accurate tire modelling is crucial in the design of HPAWD EVs.

articleTitle: Adaptive Energy Management System based on Pontryagin's Minimum Principle for Battery/Supercapacitor Electric Vehicle Considering Topographic Information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In this work an Energy Management System (EMS) is designed for Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) involving Battery/Supercapacitor (SC) for Electric Vehicles (EVs). The main aim of this research is to enhance the efficiency and performance of HESS by designing adaptive EMS based on Pontryagin's Minimum Principle (PMP) and Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) while taking real life topographical data into account. Contour Positioning System (CPS) is utilised to obtain the slope data of the road travelled by EV. The solution of an open loop constrained control problem is adjusted according to changing real time conditions to control the power allocation between battery and SC. The designed technique is tested on three real road slope conditions namely city tour, uphill and downhill under UDDS and NYCC drive cycles. The developed technique is analysed on the basis of energy consumption and the results are evaluated on the basis of battery parameters such as Root Mean Square (RMS) value of battery current and Ampere hour (Ah) throughput of the battery. The proposed technique showed a reduction of 22.98%, 23.80% and 45.28% in Ah throughput of battery in city tour, downhill and uphill conditions respectively as compared to PMP based controller. This shows that the designed Adaptive PMP (APMP) technique is able to manage the real time situations in a better way as compared to open loop PMP technique and improve the performance of battery over a wide range of road slopes and speeds.

articleTitle: Dual-MPC as Next Generation Energy Management Algorithm for Multi-Energy-Source Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Next Generation Energy Management Algorithms for multi-energy source and multi-motor electric vehicles are gaining a new degree of freedom by controlling the individual motor torques in addition to the control of the energy source distribution. With this extension, the control algorithm is gaining complexity because the energy distribution with comparable slow dynamics is coupled with the traction allocation of the motors that show very quick dynamics. In this contribution, a Dual-Model-Predictive-Control approach is shown to tackle this problem. The control concept has been evaluated within the IEEE VTS Motor Vehicles Challenge 2023.

articleTitle: The Effect of DAB Converter Series Inductor Configurations on the Transformer Interwinding Capacitance Voltage Waveform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed analysis of the voltage waveform across the transformers interwinding capacitance in an isolated dual-active-bridge converter operated with the single-phase-shift scheme. Three scenarios are analyzed, varying in the way the series inductor is connected to the transformer. It is shown that the interwinding capacitance voltage waveform variation can be eliminated by replacing the converter series inductor with either a split inductor or by using the transformer leakage inductance as the series inductor. The experimental results demonstrate the accuracy of the presented analysis with negligible off-set. Second-order resonances are observed on top of the underlying shape of the measured waveforms, and the experimental results show a reduction in its amplitude by more than a factor of 7 by exchanging the single series inductance with a split inductor or by using the transformer leakage inductance as the series inductor. Finally, it is demonstrated that the total power loss of the converter is reduced by up to 29 % when the single series inductor is exchanged with a split series inductor.

articleTitle: Optmization Algorithm for the Charging Management of Electric Vehicles in Multi-Dwelling Residential Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)

authors.preferredName: José Rui da Rocha Pinto Ferreira

abstract: This paper presents a new strategy for recharging electric vehicles in residential buildings. The proposed approach minimizes the difference between desired and final state of charge (SOC) by the end of the charging period, by adjusting the charging power for each vehicle in real-time. A non-linear optimization problem is formulated, considering the initial and final SOC, as well as available charging time, and total available power. Results were compared to a baseline and show that the proposed solution outperforms the currently most used non-optimized method, particularly in high demand scenarios, where we achieve values of 9.3% of curtailed range when compared with the non-optimized methodology.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability Analysis of Shipboard Power Electronics-Based DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Stability is one of the most relevant technical issues for extensive and safe deployment of multi-converter DC microgrids on ships. In this paper, a small-signal stability analysis based on the impedance method was performed to assess the behavior of a multi-converter, single-bus, 1kV-600kW DC microgrid conceived for ship application. The analysis allowed to evaluate the DC bus voltage stability under different operating conditions and to discriminate the effects of different system design parameters on stability. The proposed analysis was validated by time domain simulations.

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependent Evaluation of the Voltage Stability in Vehicular Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Fail-safe vehicular power systems and proper operation of safety-critical components are fundamental requirements for automated driving functions. On the other hand, the vehicular power system is getting more susceptible to disturbances. In addition, due to overlapping interferences it is increasingly difficult to determine causes of individual disturbances. Therefore, a methodology is shown for splitting superimposed disturbances by means of suitable filtering and evaluation of the voltage stability of each filtered signal. The evaluation is based on moving averaging of the filtered voltage signals over frequency-dependent time intervals. The relative frequency distribution of the averaged voltages and their position regarding to frequency-dependent voltage time limits yield stability parameters, which show the individual effect of disturbances with different frequencies on the overall voltage stability.

articleTitle: Minimizing the Operating Cost of a Hybrid Multi-Stack Fuel Cell Vehicle Based on a Predictive Hierarchical Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The operating cost of multi-stack fuel cell (FC) hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) is notably affected by the energy management strategy (EMS). For this purpose, this study proposes a predictive hierarchical (PH)-EMS to decrease the multi-stack FC-HEV operating cost. The PH-EMS consists of two levels. The first level is a Sugeno-type fuzzy logic (FL)-EMS that determines the number of active FCs for participation in an optimization level based on the vehicle's future velocity. The second level is the model predictive control (MPC) approach, which distributes the optimal power among FCs and the battery based on the number of active FCs and predicted velocity in the prediction horizon. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed EMS, the results are compared to a rule-based (RB) EMS. The results indicate that the total operating cost of the PH-EMS is 55.504% lower compared to RB-EMS.

articleTitle: Wide Bandgap-Based Inverter Prototype for Variable Speed Electrical Propulsion Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Electrification of aviation requires the utilization of wide bandgap semiconductors for power electronics inverters. Besides strict technical challenges, the inverter design must fulfill application-specific requirements related to the operation at high altitudes. In this paper, an inverter design and prototype are discussed for an electrical propulsion drive utilized in a small air taxi. The conducted Failure Mode and Effects Analysis has identified the most critical potential failure modes of the inverter that could affect the operation of the electrical drive. The design process and commissioning are conducted with a special focus on the controller performance when utilizing disturbed and faulty measurement signals. To this end, the controller performance is evaluated in a Controller-Hardware-in-the-Loop test. Moreover, the challenges concerning the common mode current and filter requirements are addressed. Design validation and examination of the interactions are carried out using test bench setup and simulation models.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Orientation Compensation for Induction Motors Based on Voltage Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The orientation accuracy of the indirect magnetic field orientation (IFOC) is greatly affected by the rotor time constant, and the orientation deviation will lead to poor torque consistency at different temperatures. In this paper, a magnetic field orientation deviation observer (FODO) and a magnetic field orientation deviation compensation controller (FODCC) are established to correct the magnetic field orientation error online. The steady-state and transient simulation results show that the FODCC can correct the magnetic field orientation error accurately, and the torque control error and magnetic field orientation error decrease obviously.

articleTitle: Intelligent Energy Management for Fuel Cell Bus Based on Enhanced Soft Actor-Critic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Energy management strategies (EMSs) directly affect the fuel economy of hybrid electric vehicles, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has become the mainstream method for energy management in recent years. This paper proposes an intelligent DRL-based EMS for an urban fuel cell bus (FCB) powered by both fuel cell and battery to improve the energy efficiency of the FCB. To begin, an enhanced soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm integrating the standard SAC algorithm with the prioritized experience replay (PER) mechanism is innovatively formulated. Then, an intelligent EMS based on the enhanced SAC algorithm is developed. After that, the superiority of the proposed EMS is evaluated in detail by comprehensive comparisons. Simulation results indicate that the proposed EMS accelerates the convergence speed by 62.79% while improving the fuel economy by 5.18% in comparison with the EMS based on standard SAC.

articleTitle: Experimental Model Identification of a Pure Electric Vehicle Using Standard Dynamometer Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The prevalence of electrified vehicles for clean and efficient transportation systems has grasped an increasing attention of many researchers and academics in the last few years. In this context, accurate, yet attainable, modeling of electric drivelines plays a significant role to ensure optimal sizing, power management, and online control of such propulsion systems. This paper proposes a systematic approach for online modeling parameters identification of electric drivelines during standard test-drives on chassis dynamometers. The proposed approach depicts real test measurements into a self-adaptive algorithm, that tunes arbitrary modeling parameters using minimal least- square scheme to converge to reference outputs congregatedly. The achieved results reveal the ability of the proposed approach to yield accurate modeling parameters of the electric motor and battery and enable an extended post-test analysis of the investigated drivelines.

articleTitle: An Accurate MTPA Control for IPMSM Considering Variations of Motor Parameters and Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Due to the inherent nonlinearity of motor parameters, employing constant motor values can lead to a reduction in motor performance and electromagnetic torque. This paper presents an improved approach by introducing a fitting model for the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) that considers variations in magnet flux linkage and stator inductance parameters caused by magnetic material saturation and temperature effects. Through direct online calculation coupled with finite element analysis (FEA), more precise calculations can be achieved for the maximum torque-per-ampere (MTPA) trajectory. Extensive simulations confirm the significant improvement in the accuracy of torque and MTPA phase advance angle estimations. Thus, enhance motor performance with the proposed accurate control method.

articleTitle: Power Harmonic Component Suppression in Case of Un-Ideal Electro-Motive Forces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: A control system to suppress power Harmonic Components (HCs) when supplying an electric grid or motor characterized by un-ideal three-phase electro-motive forces (emfs) is presented in this paper. The proposed method can be applied in case of any three-phase emfs consisting of a certain number of HCs, each of which made up of positive-, negative-, and/or zero-sequence components. Based on emf features, different three-phase reference currents can be defined in accordance with the available degrees of freedom and power HC suppression targets. These reference currents are tracked by means of a deadbeat predictive current control algorithm, which is developed in the stationary reference frame to account for a possible wide and dense current harmonic spectrum. The effectiveness of the proposed solution is verified though a simulation study, whose results confirm the validity of the proposed theoretical approach.

articleTitle: K-Means Clustering Based Urban Rail Train Operation Condition Identification Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The configuration of the stationary energy storage system (ESS) can effectively utilize the remaining regenerative braking energy in the traction power supply system of urban rail, thus achieving energy saving and emission reduction. Energy management strategy (EMS), as the top-level control of ESS, is crucially influenced by the train status in its optimal control. The traditional method of reflecting train traction or braking conditions based on the relationship between traction network voltage and substation no-load voltage is difficult to achieve accurate identification due to the differences of no-load voltage between multiple substations. Moreover, the method of directly obtaining train status requires high-performance communication between the train and the ESS. This paper proposes an operation condition identification method based on K-means clustering, which only needs to collect some ground information to achieve online identification of the overall operation conditions of trains in the power supply section. The method proposed in this paper can provide important guidance for the EMS design and optimization of stationary ESS for urban rail transit.

articleTitle: Experimental Calibration and Validation of an Average-Speed Fuel Consumption Model Based on Synthetic Driving-Cycles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Vehicle consumption models are a key element in the development of sustainable traffic monitoring and signal control systems. Leveraging innovative Intelligent Traffic Systems (ITS) technologies, we develop and validate an average-speed fuel consumption model for various vehicle types, including a 2020 Mercedes-Benz GLE 350, which is also used for experimental validation. Toward this aim, we first show and identify an instantaneous-speed fuel consumption model as an intermediate step. We then develop a unique method for generating synthetic driving-cycles by merging existing driving-cycles in the frequency domain and randomizing their features. In this way, a comprehensive database of synthetic driving-cycles, capturing diverse conditions and scenarios, is generated, enabling a robust foundation for fuel consumption analysis and comparison. Combining these results with the instantaneous-speed model, an average driving-cycle speed to fuel consumption model can be consequently calibrated. By applying this approach to different vehicle classes, the developed models facilitate accurate fuel consumption predictions, and support the optimization of traffic signal control strategies to reduce emissions and enhance energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Real World Driving Representative Cycle Generation for Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The increasing demand for eco-friendly transportation has resulted in the emergence of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). To assess the performance of HEVs, the original equipment manufacturers (OEM) have been focusing on real-world driving cycles in addition to fixed driving cycles that are defined in the regulations. Therefore, the development and validation phases with simulations or chassis dyno testing require representative driving cycle profiles that can emulate real-world driving conditions. As a result, automatic cycle generation using real-world driving patterns has become very popular in the literature. In this paper, a novel representative cycle generation method was investigated to obtain similar vehicle behavior as on-road measurements. The proposed method utilizes the data from GPS-equipped vehicles to identify the driving pattern with the parameters that impact fuel consumption and to create a synthetic cycle that represents the typical driving behavior of a given region. Two different methods, statistical-based and Markov chain-based cycle generation were compared with a reference cycle in terms of driving pattern characteristics. After testing the most representative generated cycle on a chassis dynamometer, a 0.63% deviation was obtained in terms of fuel consumption compared to the reference cycle.

articleTitle: Influence of Modification of Dual V-Shaped IPMSM Rotor Permanent Magnet Structure on Motor Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This article studies how rotor structural changes affect the performance of dual V -shaped permanent magnet motors in electric vehicles. By examining different rotor structures, it was found that adjusting the thickness and length of the inner and outer layer magnets impacts the motor's torque and efficiency. Results show that thinner, longer magnets increase torque, while thicker, shorter magnets maintain higher speeds. The outer magnet's modification has a more significant effect on performance than the inner one. This research offers insights for optimizing electric vehicle operations and improving motor design, ultimately enhancing electric car performance.

articleTitle: Review of Linear Electromagnetic Actuators for Distribution Grid Control and Protection Apparatus
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper provides a review of the state-of-the-art linear electromagnetic actuators used in power distribution grid control and protection apparatus, such as circuit breakers. Firstly, key actuation requirements of the considered application are summarized. Then, four different aspects of actuators are identified according to which actuators can be classified. Actuators known from literature are reviewed, their key operating principles are summarized, and they are classified to comparatively analyze advantages and challenges within each of those four ways of classification. The presented approach not only provides a literature review of actuators for the application at hand, but also a generalization framework by means of classification, such that the core principle of operation as well as key advantages and disadvantages of further actuator examples can be comparatively studied.

articleTitle: Energy Management and Multi-Objective Optimization of a Fuel Cell Hybrid Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Fuel cell hybrid vehicles combine the advantages of high energy density of fuel cells and higher power density of batteries. However, to efficiently manage the power sharing between the two sources, an energy management control strategy (EMS) is essential. In this contribution, an EMS along with a multi-objective optimization (MOO) is proposed for a fuel cell battery hybrid with three objectives: fuel consumption, battery energy, and drivability. The energetic macroscopic representation (EMR) is used for powertrain model and control organization that is used for development of the EMS. The main idea is to dynamically and optimally vary the power split between the fuel cell and battery by using a dynamic saturation and rate limitation. Moreover, MOO is used to optimize the boundaries offline with certain weights between the objectives. In this contribution, an influence of variation of operation boundaries on the optimization objectives is analyzed with the EUDC driving cycle. It is observed that when the fuel cell limit is reduced, the battery energy consumption increases whereas the fuel consumption reduces, while the opposite occurs when battery limit is reduced.

articleTitle: MPS Analysis of Magneto-Rheological Fluid Magnetization Anisotropies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Magneto-Rheological Fluid (MRF) started to be used for industrial applications in the last 20 years, and, from that moment on, innovative uses have been evaluated for different applications to exploit its characteristic of changing yield stress as a function of the magnetic field applied. The interest of studying the fluid-dynamic behavior of the material and the different ways the fluid could be magnetized, bringing to anisotropy in its performance has led to looking for innovative simulation strategies and approach, for obtaining a more realistic result. The paper proposes an Electro-Thermal equivalence for performing a mapping of the Magneto-Rheological Fluid put in a gap. The model, developed with the software Particle Woks, allows to visualize the effects of a non-uniform magnetization around the fluid and how much this affects the global performance of the application. The model also allows other simulations to analyze more realistic situations as having air bubbles inside the fluid and how much that affects the final global performance. The model proposed has been applied to an innovative MRF based Zero-Emissions Braking System and the output to be evaluated is the peak braking torque available at the system once the magnetization is reached. The goal is to obtain a consistent Electro-Thermal Validation of the solution developed and the braking torque being compliant with a traditional disc brake.

articleTitle: An Accumulative Method to Time Series Prediction for Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Accurately modeling and predicting the wireless channel is crucial for improving safety in various applications, particularly in vehicles, and Machine Learning (ML) plays a significant role in achieving this. In certain situations, it is necessary to establish long-distance communication for V2V communication without increasing congestion. Although beam forming is a technique for extending the range, it is critical to choose the optimal beam, and ML can assist in predicting which beam to select and estimating the power level. In this research, an ensemble learning method like Random Forest and an ML method like LSTM are utilized to construct an accumulative time series model. Each ML concept offers distinct advantages when used alone, but our accumulative approach yields superior prediction accuracy. Our accumulative approach is designed for multi-step prediction, which is more predictive than following in the case of one-step prediction. We evaluate the performance of our accumulative approach against that of the standalone algorithms.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting for Self-Supplied Tyre Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper describes the results of a study aiming at powering tyre pressure monitoring systems with tyre deformation during motion by exploiting flexible piezoelectric transducers. For this purpose, an energy harvesting system composed of a commercial macro fiber composite piezoelectric transducer and a dedicated micropower management circuit was developed and tested in realistic conditions. Measurements performed inside tyres with the support a drum test machine and a custom wireless telemetry circuit show power levels in the order of 2 mW at 40 km/h and sustainable operation of a commercial Bluetooth tyre pressure and temperature sensor. The miniature power management circuitry is implemented in a standard PCB technology in a 3 cm2 area, and has a thickness of few mm.

articleTitle: Operando Temperature Monitoring Through Optical Fiber Sensor in Lithium-Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The battery temperature evolution is closely related to the charging and discharging process, and it is important to improve the battery management. This work presents a temperature monitoring of the internal and external of the pouch cell, and different temperature characteristic points of the pouch cell under long-term cycling conditions are discussed in detail. Considering the electrochemical corrosion inside the cell, the fiber Bragg grating is selected as the temperature sensor, and the results demonstrate that the internal temperature must be closely monitored, especially for the high discharge rates.

articleTitle: A Systemic Approach for Hybrid Energy Management Strategy Based on a Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This article presents the development of a parallel hybrid Energy Management Strategy (EMS) based on a Deep Neural Network (DNN) for fuel consumption minimization. The results show that training a NN for energy management using ARTEMIS cycle optimal paths calculated with Dynamic Programming (DP) allows it to predict with high accuracy the optimal control for the lowest fuel consumption path in various normalized cycles (NEDC, WLTC etc.). Indeed, the NN based EMS was battle-tested progressively on quasi-static vehicle model using WLTC cycle as an input. The fuel consumption during a WLTC Cycle using the NN implemented in a Backward Model Algorithm is 1.5 percent higher than the DP optimal path. Future work on the study will include dynamic MIL and HIL testing to further validate the DNN on a real-time use case.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Predictive Torque Vectoring with Brake Blending for Electric Road Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The paper presents a nonlinear model predictive control algorithm for self-driving electric vehicles. The algorithm uses a nonlinear, two-track vehicle model that enables all-wheel drive torque vectoring, active front steering, and autonomous braking. The controller tracks the desired vehicle trajectory, taking into account the battery state, and enforces energy savings through regenerative braking while preventing battery overvoltage. The performance of the algorithm was tested in a high-fidelity vehicle dynamics simulator using a realistic battery model and a reference trajectory based on the Hockenheimring racetrack, showing how it increases the maximum range of the vehicle without compromising driving performance.

articleTitle: Energy-aware Time-optimal Routing of Battery Electric Trolley Trucks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Catenary overhead lines have recently drawn attention as a means of extending the range of battery electric trucks. In order to characterize the potential stemming from such an infrastructure, our paper presents a framework to optimize the routes of battery electric trolley trucks jointly with their driving and charging strategies, whereby both static and dynamic charging is possible by either stopping at a station or by connecting to the catenary line, whenever present, while driving. Specifically, we first devise a drive cycle convex optimization model to obtain a Pareto front of optimal strategies in terms of energy usage and travel time. Thereafter, we compute such Pareto fronts for all road links present on a given road network, and leverage them to frame a time-optimal routing problem accounting for battery consumption and charging as a mixed-integer linear program that can be efficiently solved with global optimality guarantees. Our results for the BeNeLux highway network show that catenary lines can significantly reduce the travel time of battery electric trolley trucks, making them a promising alternative to internal combustion engine trucks.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Braking Strategies to Improve the Energy Recovery of an Electric Vehicle Based on Cascaded H-Bridge Inverter with Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper deals with the improvement of energy recovery in a battery electric vehicle (BEV) using a cascaded H-bridge inverter with integrated battery cells (CHB-IB). Different braking strategies are defined based on the power map of the overall traction system. These strategies are simulated on a specific driving cycle. The results are compared to select the best strategies in terms of energy consumption.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of Air-Cooled Motor for UAV Using Numerical and Experimental Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper deals with the thermal analysis of air-cooled motor for UAV using numerical and experimental methods considering the structures in which the motor is attached to the UAV. The structures are classified into several cases, and then numerical and experimental analyses are performed for each case. In the numerical analysis process, the analysis results are compared for each case, and then the suitable structure that satisfies the motor stability is discussed. In the experimental analysis process, the analysis results are compared with numerical analysis results in order to confirm the validity of the numerical analysis.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Energy Management Strategy for Series Hybrid Electric Tracked Vehicle Based on Power Coordinated Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The power distribution and fuel economy of hybrid electric vehicles are greatly influenced by energy management strategies (EMSs). In this paper, a series hybrid electric tracked vehicle (SHETV) with an independent dual-side drive and a full-wave rectification is served as the research object. The EMS based on dynamic programming (DP) is first constructed to be used as the global optimal benchmark. Then, a data-driven EMS based on power coordinated control and extracting the global optimal control rules of the DP-based EMS is developed by designing the multi-layer perceptron (MLP) neural network, a filter, and a state of charge (SOC) stabilizer to predict the appropriate power distribution, ensuring that the SOC can be maintained around the initial value and the engine power output can be smoothed. Simulation results indicate that the fuel economy of the proposed EMS is improved by 10.14% compared with the strategy without extracting the global optimal control rules and reaches 89.20% of the DP-based EMS.

articleTitle: Experimental PV-Based Charging Station for e-Bikes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental charging station for e-bikes based on solar energy. The charging station is sized for a defined PV area and a number of e-bike to charge daily. A dedicate strategy ensures a minimum state of charge of the station battery all along the years. Experimental results are provided.

articleTitle: Guided Eco-Driving of Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles via Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Eco-driving of fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles (FCHEVs) is a coupled problem of speed planning and energy management, and Model predictive control (MPC) is widely used in this field. To improve the global optimality of the traditional short-horizon MPC method, this paper proposes a guided MPC system for the eco-driving of FCHEVs. A hierarchical control framework is adopted where the long-term layer provides global vehicle speed and battery energy references under traffic light scenarios and the short-term layer realizes reference trajectory following while keeping a safe and comfortable distance from the preceding vehicle. The simulation result shows that the proposed guided MPC method can achieve better fuel economy than the traditional MPC method, especially when short-term vehicle speed and battery energy are both guided.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategy Based on an Improved TD3 Reinforcement Algorithm with Novel Experience Replay
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The energy management strategy (EMS) plays an important part in the systematic control of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). In recent years, the EMS based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) receives more attention. This paper proposes an EMS based on TD3 deep reinforcement learning algorithm with novel experience replay. The experience replay is introduced to select samples via an evaluation network aiming to improve the learning ability and the convergence speed. The results show that compared with the traditional TD3-based EMS, the proposed EMS reduces the training time by 8.73% and improves the fuel economy by 2.14%.

articleTitle: Development of a Matlab Application for the Preliminary Design of Electric Propulsion Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents an application for the preliminary design of Electric Propulsion Systems (EPSs) for Electric Vehicles (EVs). It is characterized by a friendly user interface developed using the Matlab tool AppDesigner that allows the imposition of the EV performance and the evaluation of the required EPS specification. Subsequently, the preliminary design of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM) and transmission system is obtained by imposing appropriate design targets, mechanical and electromagnetic constraints and operating conditions, and selecting machine materials. The PMSM design is validated through FEA analysis. This results in a useful tool for the design of EPS components, quick and easy to use.

articleTitle: Economic Potential of V2G in Electricity Markets – A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper addresses the economic potential of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) applications in electricity markets. While V2G enabled by bidirectional charging offers flexibility to power grids, its adoption largely depends on the economic potential of stakeholders. Several papers have examined V2G revenue potential using different modeling approaches and have shown the potential for different markets. However, there is a lack of work that compares the results in terms of economic potential and classifies them at the level of geographic areas and electricity market segments. In this paper, we address this research gap by reviewing 81 publications evaluating the economic viability of V2G. Revenue potentials range widely, from approximately 8 € to 7,348 €.

articleTitle: Charging Design for Battery Electric Multiple Unit: Implementation on a Real Railway Line
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The strict environmental policies aiming to reduce emissions are changing the perspectives of mobility. Trans-portation sector is contributing in this switch, with solutions designed to be implemented to achieve the targets. Also railway sector must contribute to this change through BEMU. Some European countries have already adopted this solution, but in Italy this technology is not yet used, despite efforts in ease its implementation. This paper provides a charging solution to allow the implementation of BEMU in the Italian railway network. First, a general overview on the different charging options is given. Secondly, a power supply system is designed to solve technical criticality. Finally, a preliminary economic analysis is provided to evaluate the feasibility of the solution proposed with the actual service status.

articleTitle: Inductance and Power Losses Analysis of an Arm Inductor for a Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Researchers in the literature have investigated the optimal design of arm inductors for Modular Multilevel Converters (MMCs). However, the verification of the optimal design based on simulation is rarely provided. Therefore, this paper presents a detailed analysis and simulation of the arm inductance and power losses of an arm inductor for an MMC. The result of this study shows that the flux density is within the saturation limit, and the simulated inductance is 1.909 mH while the required inductance is 2 mH. A high accuracy of 95.4% is found between simulation and desire inductance. Furthermore, the power losses are calculated and presented separately for each part of the inductor.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Permanent Magnet Motor Performances using Different Driving Cycles for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for designing traction machines in electric vehicles that aims to achieve maximum efficiency while satisfying the necessary torque-speed requirements for selected driving cycles. The current study encompasses multiple driving cycles, specifically the US Environmental Protection Agency's (FTP) Test Schedule, the Highway Fuel Test (HWFET) Test Schedule, Dynamic Artemis Urban Driving Schedule, and Artemis 150. The suggested design method is based on deducing how a particular driving cycle disperses energy. Using a method called k-means clustering The design optimization process may be greatly sped up by characterizing the traction machine's energy efficiency at representative times during the driving cycle. The approach permits optimization with regard to these sample points, as opposed to calculating the design optimization throughout the full driving cycle, which may be time-consuming. this approach facilitates optimization in relation to these selected representative points. The capacity to considerably diminish computation time and enhance energy efficiency renders it a valuable instrument for the purpose of designing and optimizing traction machines in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: A Modified Deadbeat Predictive Flux Control for Reducing Torque Ripple at Low Modulation Ratio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified accurate deadbeat predictive flux control (M-ADPFC) to reduce the torque ripple and improve the torque tracking accuracy at low modulation ratio. A torque ripple model with discretization error compensation and low computation burden is utilized to predict the torque ripple and tracking error in the space vector modulation (SVM) process. An optimization method based on the continuous-control set model predictive control (CCS-MPC) is proposed to minimized the torque ripple. Comparative simulations validate that the proposed method has reduced torque ripple and good tracking accuracy in a wide load range at low modulation ratio.

articleTitle: Limitations of the State of Health and Health Indicators for Electric Vehicle Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Estimating the State of Health of Electric Vehicle batteries is a crucial yet challenging task. Various Health Indicators have been proposed to assess degradation, yet several of them may not be obtainable under normal operation. Additionally, battery degradation alone does not provide insights into the battery's functionality for a specific application. To address these limitations, this study analyses experimental data reflecting diverse driving conditions and evaluates the efficacy of various Health Indicators to estimate the State of Health. Results show that the value of the second peak in the Incremental Capacity curve and the use of multiple indicators produce the most accurate results. Furthermore, this study introduces a functional definition of battery degradation through the State of Function, which combines the specific driving requirements with the capacity to estimate how far the battery is from its functional End of Life. This approach provides a more comprehensive understanding of the battery's health and its ability to perform efficiently for a given application.

articleTitle: Multiple Fuzzy Adaptive Decoupled Control of High-Power Commercial Vehicular Fuel Cell Engine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This study proposes a novel method for achieving decoupled control of commercial vehicular fuel cell engines using multiple fuzzy decoupled proportion integration differentiation (MFD-PID) controller. Compared to existing approaches, this method offers advantages such as non-transfer function identification, easy implementation, and adaptability. To evaluate the efficacy of the proposed control strategy, experiments were conducted on a 60kW level high-power vehicular fuel cell system. The experiment results demonstrate that the MFD-PID outperforms conventional double PID (D-PID) and double fuzzy-PID controllers (DF -PID), reducing pressure control error by 54.2% and 28.8% compared to D-PID and DF-PID, respectively. Besides, the MFD- PID reduces air stoichiometric ratio control error by 36.4% and 7.6% compared to D-PID and DF-PID, respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Wear Rate Between Copper Impregnated Graphite and Copper
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The catenary pantograph overhead system is key to supply electrical transports such as trains. This device still requires maintenance and is subject to failures due to wear or excessive heat. It is also a multi-physical subject where many factors influence the contact properties, making it significantly complex to study. In this work, a test bench represents this links is presented. The study is focused on the volume loss, temperature, contact voltage and friction measurements obtained for a graphite impregnated copper pin. While a factorial fractional experimental design is realized, the data are used thanks to an analysis of variance to obtain the wear rate sources between five factors.

articleTitle: Fast Charge of a Battery Considering Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper aims to study the recharge time for a battery as a function of the temperature. An electro-thermal model is used for the battery to simulate the evolution of the battery temperature. The electrical parameters of the battery are dependent on the battery temperature and the state of charge. They have been characterized from an electric vehicle Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) cell. Instead of a classical Constant Current, Constant Voltage (CC-CV) technique, a current trajectory is used for charging. The goal is to recharge at maximal admissible current to be as fast as possible. The maximal admissible charge current is a function of the battery internal temperature. Simulation are performed for a 0 °C to 40°C temperature range for ambient temperature. The simulation results show that the fast charging is slower when the ambient temperature is increasing.

articleTitle: Impact of Riding Posture and Regenerative Braking on Electric Motorcycle Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of riding posture and regenerative braking on electric motorcycle energy economy is described. The motorcycle longitudinal dynamic model is first built to describe the motorcycle acceleration, tyre load transfer and energy consumption. Through energy consumption analysis based on the world motorcycle test cycle-class 3–2 (WMTC 3–2), the low riding posture can save up to 22.65% of energy consumption than the high riding posture, and regenerative braking can help to save up to 7.65% of energy consumption, which demonstrates the benefit of riding posture control and regenerative braking on energy saving. It is also demonstrated that riding posture has an impact on the rear tyre load and the available rear tyre longitudinal force. At low tyre road friction conditions, higher riding posture can provide more rear tyre longitudinal force for accelerating and regenerative braking, which improves the motorcycle dynamic performance and energy economy.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Synergy For Pure Electric Vehicles Using on-Board LiC:A Genetic Algorithm Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Development processes related to vehicles' energy storage systems added significant improvements to their performance under different operating conditions. Many researchers and scholars devoted their interests to enhancing the capabilities and effectiveness of the battery, the primary energy source of any electrified propulsion system, such as prolonging its lifetime, increasing its storage capacity, fast charging ability without any prospective degradation, and adaptability to different operating temperatures. One of the salient solutions proposed to compensate for the majority of lithium-ion batteries' shortcomings is the hybridization with another energy storage system. Lithium-ion capacitors are a powerful energy source that can be integrated with batteries to attain useful results. This paper investigates a semi-active topology between a high-fidelity model of a lithium-ion battery and an on-board lithium-ion capacitor connected to a DC-DC converter. The proposed model of a battery has been compared with real test stand data over various standardized driving cycles after an accurate estimation of the battery parameters, which showed a high degree of consistency between simulation results and actual test data. An optimization technique-based genetic algorithm is proposed to determine the optimal power synergy between the energy sources while satisfying the constraints defined to limit the drastic drop in the state of charge for both energy sources without violating driveability conditions. The optimization results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed hybridization between energy sources in extending vehicle range and reducing the depleted energy from the lithium-ion battery under different standard driving cycles.

articleTitle: Enhancing Electric Vehicle Comfort with Magnetostrictive Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The motion of electric vehicles on roads is commonly affected by vibrations arising from the unevenness of the ground and, partially, from the electric motor. This paper proposes a novel approach to harness these vibrations using an Energy Harvesting device based on magnetostrictive materials, with the primary objective of recovering otherwise wasted energy and enhancing passenger comfort. The key concept underlying this idea involves integrating the harvester between the car's body and suspensions. By doing so, the initial energy generated by the car body's vibrations is partially converted into electrical energy before reaching the suspensions, thereby leading to improved comfort. The same concept applies between the car body and the motor mounts. The performance of a prototype device has been experimentally tested under realistic dynamic mechanical stresses and the main results are presented herein.

articleTitle: Design of a Linear Generator for Energy Harvesting from Interstitial Space in Suspensions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Due to the increase in the electrification of road transport vehicles, energy harvesting technologies are being more considered. This paper investigates the possibility to introduce a permanent magnet linear generator in the interstitial space of a common suspension system. An optimized geometry described by recent papers is exploited to evaluate the efficiency of energy harvesting with a complete multi-physical finite element method simulation including the electrical circuit for harvesting and the mechanical differential equations. Poor quality and good quality road profiles are generated and the suspension with embedded generator is tested with different vehicle velocities in a multiphysics finite element simulation. The simulations point out that the output voltage of a designed single three-phase linear generator is enough for a slow recharge of a 100Ah-12V car service battery.

articleTitle: Motor Vehicle Challenge 2023: The Winning Multi-physical Energy Management Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: A rule-based energy management algorithm for multi-energy source and multi-motor electric vehicles is pre-sented. The designed solution is implemented for a vehicle with two in-wheel electric motors installed in the rear axle and one central front motor. The energy needed to power the vehicle is provided by a hybrid energy storage system with hydrogen fuel cell and battery pack. Energy consumption, battery degradation, safety constraints and derating of the vehicle performance are the main metrics of the given cost function to be minimized. The algorithm is validated with an extensive simulation stage. Different driving cycles containing typical operating conditions of the vehicle are used. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is further corroborated by winning the IEEE Motor Vehicle Challenge 2023.

articleTitle: Analysis of Communication Delays in Roadside Detection Systems for Cooperative AEB Implementation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The recent development in the framework of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) relies on the availability of ultra-fast networks for achieving low-latency communication. In fact, for the actual implementation of the Cooperative-Advanced Driving Assistance System(C-ADAS) based on V2X communication, a limited delay can be tolerated for safety-critical control algorithms such as Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB). This work proposes a detailed evaluation of the latency involved in a roadside detection system based on a commercial thermal camera aimed at communicating with surrounding connected vehicles through Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol. In particular, the focus is pointed on the proposed communication architecture that has been designed and implemented, as well as on how delay can affect the performance of an AEB control logic implementation, highlighting limitations and possible ways to cope with this issue. Experimental results show that the SG-based communication architecture proposed limits E2E latency below 200 ms, which, on the basis of simulation tests for a large public transportation vehicle, still represents a relevant amount of time for safety-critical ADAS implementation, thus requiring some methodologies for delay compensation.

articleTitle: Development of a Equivalent Impedance Network Reproducing the Impedance of Electric Vehicles During Active DC Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Beside the ongoing vehicle electrification, a massive expansion of the charging infrastructure is present. These charging stations are operated at rising power levels and increasing voltages of up to 800V focusing on passenger vehicles and up to 1500V for heavy duty vehicles. Beside the speed up of the charging process these technology trends have a large impact on the electromagnetic emissions of the DC charging process which must fulfill the requirements addressed in the standard IEC 61851-21-2 [1]. For measuring the emissions, the charging station has to be operated in a realistic operation point. Therefore, an adequate load modelling of the impedance of an electric vehicle can be used to gain realistic results. Since the vehicle impedances in the frequency range between 9 kHz respectively 150 kHz and 30 MHz are not known, in this work an inductive decoupled impedance measurement procedure [2], [3] is presented and applied to the DC-charging setup. For data acquisition in total three electric vehicles with different battery capacities are measured during active DC-Charging operation. In a further step the impedance of one vehicle is chosen to design a passive impedance network reproducing its impedance at the DC charging port. Using this impedance network more realistic emission results can be gained during operation of a DC charging station.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Torque Estimation Algorithms for Switched Reluctance Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Switched reluctance machines are gaining importance due to their low cost, simple construction, and non-use of rare earth magnets. However, for the development of advanced torque controllers, accurate torque estimation is crucial, especially under varying load conditions. There are different torque estimation methods, which fall into different well-established classes, however, the characterization of their performance and operating conditions are not well known. This paper provides a comparative study of the most significant estimation algorithms: average torque, analytical and area approximation estimators. To assess the performance of these algorithms, a set of numerical simulations is presented and their results are compared based on signal similarity criteria. Results show a better performance when using the area approximation algorithm in comparison with the other two.

articleTitle: A SOC Estimation Method for Internal Short Circuit Battery Based on EKF-FFRLS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are usually connected in series in large-scale battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and the safety operation of battery packs has become a hotspot. The accurate estimation of the State of Charge (SOC) is a key factor in ensuring the safe and reliable operation of battery packs. The SOC of the battery is important for the diagnosis of internal short circuit (ISC) fault, while the external characteristics of the ISC fault are not obvious, and the continuous micro short circuit discharge of the battery brings difficulties to the accurate estimation of the SOC. This paper proposes a SOC estimation method for ISC battery, which combines Extended Kalman Filtering (EKF) and Recursive Least Squares with Forgetting Factor (FFRLS). An equivalent circuit model of the ISC battery is established first and the FFRLS algorithm is used to identify model parameters. Then, the EKF algorithm and the model parameters obtained through identification are employed to estimate SOC. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively estimate the battery SOC under the FUDS discharging condition and the maximum estimation error of SOC is 0.9%.

Author Keywords: Recursive least squares with forgetting factor

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Pure H2/O2 Fuel Cell–Battery Hybrid Systems for Long-Range AUVs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: As platform, communication, navigation, and control technologies, which have long been considered core technologies of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), have developed, there have been various efforts to improve the operational time of existing battery-based AUVs. Although research on hydrogen fuel cell systems with high energy density, air-independent propulsion, and low noise began in the early 2000s, many technological challenges remain. In this paper, we first present prototypes of overseas UUV developments powered by fuel cells. The main characteristics and design considerations of the fuel cell system for unmanned submarines identified through development cases and conceptual studies are then presented. Finally, the system implementation and performance test results are introduced.

articleTitle: Efficient Optimization-Based Control of a Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicle with Torque Vectoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper proposes a practical strategy to easily take advantage of both torque allocation and power split toward low hydrogen consumption and component degradation for multi-motor hydrogen hybrid electric vehicles. Sigmoid-shaped functions are identified from optimal torque allocation maps using torque vectoring to reduce tire losses. A predictive rule-based power split controller is derived from optimal control, only necessitating an estimate of the cycle power distribution. The proposed method is analyzed and compared to the strategies of other participants of the 2023 IEEE VTS Motor Vehicles Challenge, revealing that despite its simplicity, the proposed strategy is robust and efficient.

articleTitle: Ensuring Customer Satisfaction on Long Distance Train Journeys: An Indian Railways Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Imagine embarking on a long journey, only to realize that a smartphone charger or the smart LED display in front of your seat is not functional. Ensuring customer satisfaction is important in building a loyal customer base and making the customer feel satisfied about the quality of their journey. This paper probes a significant lacuna within the Indian Railways that pushes the onus on the passenger to report a problem and then follow it up until resolution. Myriad ways of reporting problems confuse travelers. This paper advocates collection of passenger comfort data thru a smart phone application. An initial categorization of the problem is explained followed by building an intelligent system that solves problems quickly. Smarter resolution, with active participation of on-board staff and ways to incentivize the passenger reporting the problem are suggested. Unique customer satisfaction metrics and factors affecting them with examples to apply in the railways are explored. Equipment failure data gathered via the app, could be integrated with asset management databases for predicted maintenance. Finally, a staged implementation plan is proposed that uses Machine Learning (ML) models for life cycle assessment of parts.

articleTitle: Round-Trip Energy Efficiency and Energy-Efficiency Fade Estimation for Battery Passport
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The battery passport is proposed as a method to make the use and remaining value of batteries more transparent. The future EU Battery Directive requests this passport to contain the round-trip energy efficiency and its fade. In this paper, an algorithm is presented and demonstrated that estimates the round-trip energy efficiency of a battery pack. The algorithm identifies round trips based on battery current and SoC and characterizes these round trips based on certain conditions. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{D}$</tex> efficiency maps are created as a function of the conditions ‘temperature’ and 'RMS C-rate‘. The maps are parameterized using multiple linear regression, which allows comparison of the efficiency under the same conditions. Analyzing data from three battery-electric buses over a period of 3.5 years reveals an efficiency fade of up to 0.86 percent point.

articleTitle: An Optimal Approach to Energy Management of a Hybrid Fuel-Cell Competition Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In this paper, we design an energy management control system to improve powertrain efficiency and optimize the amount of fuel used in a route-based scenario by a hybrid fuel cell vehicle. To reach this goal a complete tank-to-wheel model is developed; under the assumption of a known scenario the speed profile that minimizes the required energy to complete the test is computed and a controller able to handle the power request is designed. In particular, a Model Predictive Control architecture is used to split the power request between the primary and the secondary power source (fuel cell and supercapacitor). To develop and test the proposed energy management control system, the hydrogen prototype IDRAkronos is used. The vehicle is designed and built by the Team H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>politO of the Politecnico di Torino to join the Shell Eco-Marathon competition.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multi-Objective Optimization Strategy for Real-Time Energy Management of Fuel Cell Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In this study, we propose an adaptive multi-objective optimization energy management strategy for optimizing the instantaneous power split in fuel-cell/battery electric vehicle. The optimization objectives include improving fuel economy, maintaining the state of charge of battery at a medium level, and extending fuel cell lifespan by suppressing dramatic changes in fuel cell power. The weighting factors of the objective functions can be dynamically adjusted based on real-time operating data of the hybrid power system. The proposed strategy is simulated and compared with a rule-based strategy under four different driving cycles. The results demonstrate that our strategy can reduce fuel consumption in varying degrees, and it allows the fluctuations in state of charge of battery to be always controlled within a reasonable range. The most outstanding aspect of this strategy is that it enables an over 80% reduction on the average variation rate of fuel cell power.
